events.title: Intel 8088 introduced
events.summary: Intel introduced the 8088 microprocessor in July 1979 — a cost-reduced 16-bit x86 variant with an 8-bit external bus.
events.about: IBM chose the 8088 for the original PC because its 8-bit data bus worked with cheaper existing peripheral chips — while software still targeted 16-bit x86 instructions. The 8088 launched the PC clone industry and the entire DOS/Windows software ecosystem on Intel architecture.

narrative.whyChosen: The 8088 was the CPU inside the IBM PC 5150 — the seed of the x86 PC standard.
narrative.whyImportant: IBM's choice made 8088/x86 the default architecture for personal computing.
narrative.problemSolved: PC designs needed 16-bit computing at a price point 8-bit peripherals could support.
